subject: Prorate & billing examples for mixed short calls + long-context pilot
messages:
From: Jacob Meyers <procurement@heliumhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-29T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify: how fractional tokens & minimums will land on invoices for pilot

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we finalize the pilot term sheet, our finance team needs a clear worked example showing how you bill when we have: a) lots of short synchronous requests (2–30 tokens), b) occasional long-context summarization calls (~8–12k tokens), and c) streaming assistant sessions where the user keeps a chat open for long periods.

Specific asks:
- Show the rounding / quantum rules you apply per request (if any) for short calls vs streaming vs long-context generation.
- Demonstrate how KV cache reuse reduces billed tokens for follow-ups in the same conversation, and whether that interacts with any per-request minimums.
- Provide a realistic invoice snippet for a month where we had ~220k short requests, 2 long-context jobs of 10k generations each, and 1 streaming session with intermittent heartbeats.

I attached a sample usage CSV and the current term sheet draft. If you can send a one-pager playbook with examples and the invoice impact, that would help speed approvals.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

Jacob
Sr. Procurement
Helium Health

Attachments: pilot_usage_sample.csv (CSV), term_sheet_draft.pdf (PDF)

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Meyers <procurement@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-29T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify: how fractional tokens & minimums will land on invoices for pilot

Jacob —

Thanks for the clear list. I've looped in Ben (pricing/math) and Vanessa (billing/pilot ops) so we can produce a concise playbook and a sample invoice. Below are the high-level rules we propose for the pilot (we'll formalize in the attached one-pager):

- Per-request quantum: short synchronous requests are rounded up to the nearest 20-token quantum (to reduce meter noise).
- Long-context jobs: billed per token produced/consumed; we apply the same 20-token quantum on the initial write call but, for multi-part generation we sum and then apply the quantum to the aggregated job to avoid double-rounding.
- Streaming sessions: we apply a small per-minute heartbeat charge when idle OR a per-call minimum of 100 tokens if activity is bursty (whichever yields lower customer cost).
- KV cache: prefix tokens satisfied from cache are not billed. For follow-ups that reuse KV, only the new tokens are counted. KV reuse can materially reduce billed tokens for conversational pilots; we'll show two worked examples.

We'll put the worked math and an invoice snippet in the playbook and share within 24 hours. Can you confirm if you want the sample invoice in USD and whether tax-inclusive figures are preferred?

Thanks,
Stephanie
Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none (will attach playbook)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-29T13:21:00Z
Subject: RE: Clarify: how fractional tokens & minimums will land on invoices for pilot

Steph / Vanessa —

Draft math to use in the playbook (simple, copyable):

Scenario assumptions (for sample invoice):
- Short requests: 220,000 calls, avg 12 tokens generated per call, unit price $0.00008 per token (list price)
- Long-context jobs: 2 jobs x 10,000 tokens generated each = 20,000 tokens
- Streaming session: 1 session, active generation total 14,000 tokens across the day, with idle heartbeats adding 1,200 tokens equivalent under our per-minute model

Rules we apply (explicit):
1) Quantum rounding: after we compute tokens per request, we round up to next 20-token quantum for that request category. Example: a 12-token call is billed as 20 tokens.
2) Aggregation guard for long jobs: for a single long job we aggregate all sub-requests and then apply quantum once to the aggregate to avoid repeated rounding. So 10,000 tokens stays 10,000 and then is rounded to the nearest 20 (10,000 is divisible; no extra).
3) Streaming: we charge actual tokens while active; during idle periods we bill per-minute heartbeat equivalent at 5 tokens/minute (capped by a 100-token minimum per session for bursty sessions).
4) KV cache: cached prefix tokens are zero-cost. Billing only counts the delta tokens that are not satisfied from cache. If a follow-up consumes 30 tokens but 18 tokens were satisfied from the KV, you bill on 12 tokens (then apply quantum rounding).

Worked invoice numbers (USD) — quick sketch: 
- Short calls: 220,000 calls * billed 20 tokens each = 4,400,000 billed tokens * $0.00008 = $352.00
- Long jobs: 20,000 tokens billed * $0.00008 = $1.60
- Streaming: 15,200 tokens billed * $0.00008 = $1.216
- Subtotal tokens: 4,435,200 tokens -> $354.816 -> round on invoice to $354.82

Notes: the quantum causes most cost in very high-volume, very-short calls; we include a monthly minimum credit if pilot is below $500 and will waive for a signed pilot. Also, we can offer a 10% pilot discount applied at invoice time (negotiable).

I'll annotate the one-pager with these numbers and a table showing a follow-up with KV reuse.

Ben
Pricing Analytics
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: math_snippets.txt — short examples for the playbook)

From: Jacob Meyers <procurement@heliumhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify: how fractional tokens & minimums will land on invoices for pilot

Thanks — this helps a lot. Two quick clarifications: 
1) For the short-call math, you rounded 12 -> 20 tokens. Will that be visible on the usage CSV (i.e., do you expose pre- and post-rounding token columns)? Our finance team needs to reconcile back to raw API logs.
2) For KV cache: if cache satisfactions are not billed, do you ever subtract previous billed charges if we enabled cache retroactively? We're likely to enable warm prefixes after our first week of pilot.

Also, the pilot discount you mentioned — is that applied on gross billed tokens or on the dollar total?

Jacob

On a second note, could you include a worked example where short calls are batched (we might use client-side micro-batching) and show the delta vs unbatched calls?

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Meyers <procurement@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-31T17:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify: how fractional tokens & minimums will land on invoices for pilot

Jacob —

Great questions. Short answers up front:
- Usage CSV: yes, we include both raw token counts (from your API logs) and billed token counts (post-quantum/rounding) as separate columns so reconciliation is straightforward.
- Retroactive cache: we do not retroactively refund previously billed tokens when cache is enabled; instead we apply a forward-looking credit if the change materially reduces costs during the billing period (we can treat this as a one-off invoice credit during pilot). We'll document the process in the playbook.
- Pilot discount: typically applied to the invoice dollar subtotal (post-quantum/do-not-double-round), not to raw tokens. We can structure it either as percentage off invoice or a fixed pilot credit — will confirm in the term sheet.

Per your batching ask, attached is a one-page playbook (proration-playbook-v1.pdf) with:
- worked examples showing unbatched vs client-side micro-batched short calls (12 tokens * 100 calls vs batched 1200 tokens where quantum applied once)
- KV reuse examples (before/after) and how we surface both raw and billed columns in the CSV
- a sample invoice snippet in USD with the 10% pilot discount applied as a dollar line item

Next steps: if this looks good, I can turn the playbook into a slightly expanded pilot appendix to the term sheet and include the explicit waiver for the monthly minimum during the 60-day pilot. Would you prefer a short call to walk the finance team through the CSV columns?

Thanks — attaching: proration-playbook-v1.pdf

Steph
Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proration-playbook-v1.pdf (1 page)
